headline: Hot inflation print puts another RBA rate hike firmly on the table, while Gulf states race to prevent a US-Iran war resumption and oil spikes 2% on the tension.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara bounced 3.82% today in a solid session for lithium stocks. No single news catalyst — more of a relief rally after recent weakness. The long-term lithium demand story (EVs, batteries) is intact, but the share price is still down over 55% on your cost base, reflecting how tough the lithium market has been. Nothing's fundamentally changed yet.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: The AI ETF gained 1.28% today, riding positive sentiment from last night's strong NASDAQ session and Google's announcement of its new Genie 4 world-simulation AI model. Tech and AI names broadly lifted, which flows directly into this ETF.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Emerging markets ticked up 0.61% today. The slightly firmer Aussie dollar (now 70.35 US cents) and last night's solid US market session helped sentiment toward higher-risk assets like emerging market equities.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google rose 0.84% last night on the NASDAQ, helped by news Alphabet is expanding its cloud infrastructure ahead of its upcoming earnings report and the launch of its impressive Genie 4 AI model. Markets seem cautiously optimistic heading into earnings, though one Seeking Alpha piece warned the results could 'burst the AI bubble' — worth watching.

movers.name: DHHF (BetaShares Diversified)
movers.note: DHHF edged up 0.34% today — quiet session, broadly tracking the flat ASX 200. Nothing specific to this holding; it's just riding the market's mild moves.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS gained 0.35% today on the ASX, tracking last night's strong US session where the NASDAQ jumped 1.18% and the S&P 500 rose 0.6%. US stocks broadly lifted, and this ETF captures that.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG edged up 0.17% in a quiet session. It holds a broad mix of Australian and international shares, so its gentle rise reflects the mixed picture — flat ASX but a positive overnight US session feeding through.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft slipped just 0.24% last night — barely a blip. The market is holding its breath ahead of Microsoft's Q1 earnings report (due very soon), with all eyes on Azure cloud growth and AI capital spending. The slight dip looks like pre-earnings caution, not a structural concern.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two fell 1.02% last night, weighed down by ongoing uncertainty around the GTA 6 release timeline — reports are swirling about a possible delay into 2027. Adding to the noise, Rockstar Games workers are reportedly preparing to vote on unionisation right as GTA 6 is set to launch. Bank of America still rates it a buy ahead of a 'GTA 6-fueled earnings boom', so the long-term case is intact — but there's real execution risk here.

watch_today.title: MSFT earnings imminent — Azure growth is the key number
watch_today.detail: Microsoft reports Q1 earnings imminently (US time tonight or very soon). Wall Street is laser-focused on Azure cloud growth and how much Microsoft is spending on AI infrastructure. Last night's tiny 0.24% dip looks like pre-earnings nerves. You're sitting on a solid ~20% gain on this holding — if Azure beats expectations, this could run further. Hold tight and watch the numbers.

watch_today.title: GOOG earnings also approaching — Genie 4 launch a positive signal
watch_today.detail: Alphabet is expanding cloud infrastructure and just launched Genie 4 (a new AI model for real-time interactive simulations — think AI that can build interactive virtual environments on the fly). That's bullish for the long-term thesis. Earnings are coming up and sentiment is cautiously positive, though one analyst warns results could disappoint AI hype. Your GOOG position is in the black — hold and watch the print.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 delay fears and union vote adding risk
watch_today.detail: Take-Two dropped 1% last night as GTA 6 delay rumours (possibly pushed to 2027) and a looming Rockstar worker unionisation vote stirred concern. You're already down ~6.75% on this position. Bank of America still calls it a buy, and the GTA 6 supercycle thesis remains intact IF the game launches. For a long-term holder, this is uncomfortable but not a reason to sell — the payoff when GTA 6 hits should be enormous. Sit tight, but keep watching release date news closely.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike now looking likely in November — watch your mortgage
watch_today.detail: Australia's inflation surged to 4.3% — well above what the RBA wants. CommBank economists are now forecasting a November rate hike, and the AFR is talking about back-to-back rises. If you have a variable rate mortgage, budget for another increase. For your portfolio, higher rates are a slight headwind for growth stocks and ETFs short-term, but don't change the long-term case.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX bounced hard today — long-term outlook still challenged
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals jumped 3.82% today, which is welcome, but you're still down over 55% on this position. There's no fundamental change in the lithium market yet — prices remain weak. For a long-term holder, this is a position to hold only if you believe in the multi-year EV battery demand story. Don't read too much into one good day.

watch_today.title: Oil spiking on US-Iran war fears — watch energy costs
watch_today.detail: Crude oil jumped over 2% to US$101.93 a barrel as the US reportedly warned Gulf allies of a possible short, intense renewal of conflict with Iran after the midterm elections. Gulf states are scrambling to broker a peace deal. If oil stays elevated, expect petrol prices to rise and broader inflation to stay sticky — which feeds back into that RBA rate hike risk.

world.summary: The biggest global stories today centre on a dangerous escalation in US-Iran tensions driving oil higher, the Trump administration's aggressive push to challenge election integrity ahead of US midterms, and Gulf states racing to prevent renewed conflict in the Middle East.

stories.title: US warns Gulf allies of possible renewed Iran war after midterms
stories.why_it_matters: The US has privately warned Gulf states — including Saudi Arabia and the UAE — that it may launch a 'short, intense' military campaign against Iran once the midterm elections are over. Iran is responding by warning of 'new realities', while Gulf nations are frantically working on a multi-part peace deal to head off the conflict. This is a major escalation: it's already pushed oil above US$100 a barrel (up 2% today), and a renewed war near the Strait of Hormuz — the world's most important oil shipping lane — could send prices far higher. That means higher petrol prices and more inflation pressure globally.

stories.title: Trump administration moves to block hundreds of ballots from alleged non-citizen voters
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has formally asked Washington State to set aside more than 400 ballots it claims were cast by suspected non-citizen voters, ahead of the November midterm elections. Trump has also offered cash rewards to anyone who can prove voter fraud. Legal experts say it's highly unusual — and likely unlawful — for the federal government to intervene in state-run elections this way. California officials looked into Trump's similar claims there and found no evidence to support them. This is a significant escalation in Trump's long-running efforts to cast doubt on election results before votes are even counted.

stories.title: Gulf states racing to broker US-Iran peace deal before midterms
stories.why_it_matters: Saudi Arabia, the UAE and other Gulf nations are working urgently on a multi-part peace package to prevent the US from resuming military action against Iran. The deal reportedly involves Iranian concessions on its nuclear programme in exchange for sanctions relief. The clock is ticking — the fear is that once US midterm elections pass, the window for diplomacy closes fast. For ordinary people, the stakes are simple: if this fails and war resumes near the Persian Gulf, energy prices globally will spike sharply.

stories.title: US midterm election integrity battle heating up
stories.why_it_matters: Legal experts are warning that the Trump administration's attempts to make federal cases out of state election disputes are legally dubious and constitutionally problematic — states run their own elections, and federal interference is highly restricted. Meanwhile, local election officials in California who examined Trump's specific claims about non-citizen voters found no evidence supporting them. With midterms weeks away, the battle over who gets to vote — and who counts the votes — is intensifying in ways that could shape US political stability for years.

stories.title: Oil hits US$101.93 — highest in months as Iran tensions flare
stories.why_it_matters: Crude oil (WTI) jumped 2% last night to US$101.93 a barrel, driven almost entirely by the US-Iran war warning headlines. This is the clearest market signal yet that traders are pricing in real risk of Middle East disruption. For Australians, higher oil means higher petrol prices within weeks, and it adds to the inflation picture that's already pushing the RBA toward more rate hikes. Gold, usually a safe haven in these moments, actually dipped 0.62% to US$4,049 — suggesting some traders are selling gold to fund other bets.

politics.summary: A hot inflation print — 4.3% annually — is dominating Australian domestic news today, with CommBank economists now forecasting a November RBA rate hike. The Albanese government also passed landmark online safety legislation through the House.

stories.title: Australia's inflation surges to 4.3% — fifth rate hike of the year now likely
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's inflation rate jumped to 4.3% in the latest quarterly reading — well above the RBA's 2-3% target band and higher than most economists expected. CommBank economists are now explicitly forecasting a rate hike at the RBA's November meeting, and the AFR is flagging the possibility of back-to-back rises. That means Australians with variable rate mortgages should prepare for another increase to their repayments. It also signals the RBA believes the economy is still running too hot despite previous hikes.

stories.title: Albanese's Digital Duty of Care Bill passes the House of Representatives
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government's Digital Duty of Care Bill has passed the lower house, targeting serious online harms. One of the most notable provisions would ban AI chatbots from forming 'emotional intimacy' with users — essentially stopping apps from manipulating users into parasocial relationships with AI companions. The bill also places new obligations on social media platforms to protect users, particularly minors. It still needs to pass the Senate. Critics, including some tech industry voices, warn that poorly designed regulation could give governments too much power over online speech.

stories.title: Opposition blasts Albanese over workplace breastfeeding changes
stories.why_it_matters: Liberal Senator Michaelia Cash has publicly attacked the Albanese government over proposed workplace changes that would extend breastfeeding protections to biological men — a reference to trans-inclusive workplace legislation. The debate reflects ongoing culture-war tensions in Australian politics ahead of the next federal election cycle. It's a politically charged issue with both sides playing to their bases.

stories.title: Government backs down on aspects of internet regulation laws
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government has retreated on some elements of its internet regulation package, signalling it's struggling to get all proposed online safety measures through parliament. The back-down comes even as the broader Digital Duty of Care Bill passes the lower house, suggesting the government is making concessions to secure Senate crossbench support. The full scope of what was walked back wasn't specified in available reports.

ai.summary: Google unveiled its impressive Genie 4 world-simulation AI model, while AI regulation debates are heating up globally and in Australia. A notable benchmark report also showed Google's Gemini 4 Argon trailing rivals for coding tasks.

stories.title: Google launches Genie 4 — AI that can build interactive virtual worlds in real time
stories.why_it_matters: Google has announced Genie 4, its latest 'world model' — an AI that can generate fully interactive, real-time simulated environments from a simple prompt or image. Think of it as AI that doesn't just draw a picture of a game world, but actually builds a playable, interactive version of it on the fly. This is a significant step toward AI that can create entire virtual experiences without human developers, with obvious implications for gaming, simulation, training and virtual reality. It's also a boost for the GOOG and GXAI.AX investment thesis.

stories.title: Gemini 4 Argon ranked well behind Claude and GPT-6 for Android coding
stories.why_it_matters: Google itself has acknowledged that its Gemini 4 Argon model — designed for Android coding tasks — currently ranks significantly behind Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's GPT-6 on standard benchmarks. This is a rare public admission of competitive weakness from Google in the AI race. It suggests that while Google is making bold moves (like Genie 4), it's still playing catch-up to rivals in some core AI coding and reasoning applications. Worth watching for GOOG holders.

stories.title: NVIDIA and Meta expand collaboration on 'Muse' AI model family
stories.why_it_matters: NVIDIA and Meta have announced an expanded partnership on the 'Muse' family of AI models, which are designed to generate and understand multimodal content — meaning they can work across text, images, video and audio together, rather than just one format at a time. This deepens the integration between two of the world's most powerful AI hardware and software players, and signals that large-scale AI model development is increasingly a team sport between chip makers and software giants.

stories.title: Australia moves to ban AI 'emotional intimacy' in digital duty of care laws
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's new Digital Duty of Care Bill, which just passed the House of Representatives, includes a specific provision banning AI apps from building 'emotional intimacy' with users. This is aimed squarely at AI companion apps and chatbots that encourage users to form deep personal or romantic bonds with an artificial intelligence — a growing concern among mental health experts and regulators worldwide. Platforms that allow this would face legal liability. It puts Australia at the forefront of regulating the psychological impact of AI, not just its data privacy risks.

stories.title: AI regulation debate intensifies globally ahead of US midterms
stories.why_it_matters: Pressure to regulate AI is building globally, with US lawmakers ramping up proposals ahead of the November midterms. Two competing arguments are dominating: one camp says regulation should focus purely on harm (e.g. deepfakes, bias, safety failures) rather than the technology itself; the other warns that any regulation risks becoming a tool for government control over information. For investors in AI-exposed stocks like GOOG, MSFT, and GXAI.AX, regulatory outcomes in the US and Australia will shape how freely these companies can operate over the next decade.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 was virtually flat today, slipping just 0.03% to close at 8,847 — essentially unmoved. Last night in the US it was a much stronger session: the NASDAQ surged 1.18% and the S&P 500 gained 0.6%, driven by tech optimism and strong AI-related news. Oil spiked over 2% on US-Iran war fears, gold dipped slightly, and the Aussie dollar crept up to 70.35 US cents.

sport.summary: It's Rugby League World Cup season — Australia's Bati squad is building for their next challenge, the Roosters claimed the NRL Grand Final in a thriller, and the AFL trade period is heating up with Walker saga drama and 2027 lineup speculation.

stories.title: Roosters win NRL Grand Final 19-18 over Knights in a one-point thriller
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters edged the Newcastle Knights 19-18 in one of the closest NRL Grand Finals in recent memory — a single-point margin. It's a heartbreaker for Knights fans and a thrilling championship for the Roosters. The game went down to the wire at Accor Stadium.

stories.title: Rugby League World Cup Week 2 wrap — Jamayne Isaako primed for Fiji Bati
stories.why_it_matters: The Rugby League World Cup is in full swing with Week 2 done. Jamayne Isaako is reportedly fired up and in form for the Fiji Bati, having just had a homecoming parade before linking back up with the squad. Week 3 fixtures are set to air on Channel 7 — check listings for times.

stories.title: Adam Walker saga: 'most disappointing' details emerge — and a Rabbitohs twist
stories.why_it_matters: The Adam Walker transfer saga is dragging on with Fox Sports' Ennis revealing what he calls the 'most disappointing' aspect of the situation, while also sharing a 'gut feeling' about which club ultimately signs him. There's also a surprising South Sydney Rabbitohs angle emerging. No confirmed destination yet — but the rumour mill is loud heading into the off-season.

stories.title: AFL trade period: every club's predicted 2027 lineup, plus Walker-to-Bunnies whispers
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL trade and draft period is generating plenty of heat. Fox Sports has mapped out every club's predicted 2027 lineup — with the Roosters (Sydney) facing a halves crisis and the North Sydney Bears reportedly landing a maiden spine for their new era. The NRL transfer tracker is also logging every confirmed signing and exit across all clubs as the off-season market opens up.

stories.title: Jannik Sinner tipped to dominate Australian Open, says former world No. 4
stories.why_it_matters: A former world No. 4 has predicted Jannik Sinner will be the dominant force at the Australian Open in January — big news for local tennis fans planning to tune in or attend. Sinner has been in superb form on the tour and is being widely regarded as the pre-tournament favourite ahead of the Melbourne summer slam.
